segments.he: סיפרו לפני מוהרנ"ת ז"ל שהמגיד מדובנא אומר בתוכחותו שאין ניצוץ אור "עס איז נטא קוין פונק" ענה מהרנ"ת ז"ל ואמר יש ניצוץ אבל אין מנפח שיוכל לנפח היטב את הניצוץ "זו פינק איז דא נאר עס איז ניטא קיין בלאזער ער זאל ציא בלאזין דעם פונק" (היינו שכל לב איש הישראלי כוסף ובוער להשי"ת רק שהי' שהוא בעפרוריות התאוות והעצבות וטרדות וכו' וחסר צדיק שיוכל לנפח את העפריות ולעורר את הניצוץ בלב כל אחד שיבעור להשי"ת.
segments.en: Before his passing, there was an event: the lamp by which he studied went out. He kept going back to it to see if it was burning — and saw that it had gone out again — and he kept relighting it. He sensed there was a great serpent there, and the serpent fled to the other room — the room that today is where the men stand at the holy grave. He went after it, and when he came to the inner room by the holy grave, he saw Reb Shimon bar Yochai sitting there. And Rashbi said to him: "Know that the time has come for you to depart from the world. Your place is in Tzfas. And because you were always here with me in Torah and the service of G-d, you have the merit that I appeared to you before your passing. In three more days you will be taken from the world — therefore travel to Tzfas and give instructions to your household." And so it was: on that day the driver came, and Chacham Yechezkel traveled with him to Tzfas, gave his instructions to his household — and was taken from the world in peace. And there is a beautiful story about Chacham Yechezkel who went with other Kohanim to the burial cave of Aharon HaKohen — but I do not remember it well enough to record it properly.
